verdict: depot.render.js is a strong file that clears the bar set by production.render.js on substance: it is a genuinely pure string builder (zero DOM/listener/await/.from/.rpc hits, only a relative import of routes.js), it never throws for any view shape I could construct, it escapes every player string correctly, and it declares an authority everywhere two files could disagree — routes.js owns MERIDIAN_TARIFF_MULT/TIME_MULT, depot.js owns bays/cap/reach and its own why/fix, rigs.data.js owns the rarity ladder, index.js's cargoText owns resource names. Its integration claims are checkable and I checked them: every data-mt action it emits (close/tab/refresh/found/tariff/register/quote/meridian/dispatch/settle/repair) is handled by index.js, all seven pinned field ids are read by fieldVal(), contracts.js:693 really does deliberately skip the blacklist column, carrierBlock() really does append Meridian, sql/038_transport_companies.sql really exists. It records rejected designs with their cost (namespace vs named import as a link-failure hedge; no vehicle-id text box; no module-level form memory; no second rarity or resource table; sorting on a copy) and it hardens a hole production.render.js leaves open by whitelisting rarityColor to a hex literal instead of merely escaping it. What keeps it from a win is the one property this repo prizes most: the comments make four factual claims about the rest of the feature that are false as shipped, and one of them is also a render defect.
biggest_gap: The file asserts 'index.js has already trimmed it to 160 chars' about view.error and therefore prints it raw; index.js never trims it (no slice(0,160) anywhere in index.js; S.error = String(r.why || r.error) at index.js:191). renderTransport({error:'Z'.repeat(5000)}) emits all 5000 characters into the banner. Either trim defensively here (the file already does exactly that for its own caught errors, str(e.message).slice(0,160)) or delete the assertion — a comment claiming an upstream guarantee that does not exist is the failure this file's own header is organised against.

DEFECTS: (1) view.error is rendered untrimmed -- 5000 chars in, 5000 chars out -- against the comment at line 401-408 asserting index.js trimmed it; index.js has no slice(0,160). (2) Two file:line citations are stale and point at unrelated code as shipped: 'index.html:79921-79926' (the real 'Name the real error instead of guessing at a cause' scar is at index.html:79943) and 'index.html:164244' (the real Hand-hauled returns are index.html:164476 and 164479). The underlying facts are true; the line numbers are ~230 lines off and the rubric names stale line references as a failure. (3) quoteForm()'s '⚠ KNOWN DEFECT' block (lines 731-742) says view.form 'is optional and absent today' -- index.js:604 already sets form:{from,to,resId,units,carrierId} and index.js:86-95 explains it was added at this file's request, so the documented defect no longer exists. (4) lotBlock()'s '🪝 DEAD HOOK' comment (686-696) says view.lot 'is NOT in the pinned view shape, so this block renders nothing today' -- index.js:603 sets lot: lotBlock(b) and returns exactly the {vehicleId,name,rarityName,rarityColor,condition} shape the comment predicts, so the hook is live. (5) Acceptance 11's ⚠-flagged unknown resource only fires on a structured c.cargo array; index.js sends only cargoText (a joined string, index.js cargoText()), so an unknown id shows as a raw id but is never ⚠-flagged in the path that actually runs. The file documents this honestly at 1013-1030, but the criterion is not met end to end. No SQL, no ledger, no index.html edit (git shows the file tracked and unmodified; _synckcheck.mjs not applicable), no _convoyCanSend reference, no hardcoded economy number (charter.startup renders '—' when _opEcon returns nothing), Garage rigs are explicitly kept off the fleet rail (garageCard, 533-567), no discord/webhook/img/upload tokens.
